record.paper_title: A Few Problems on Monodromy and Discriminants
record.context_brief: real obstructions to chains of formal surgeries
record.original_question: Let f:(C^n,R^n,0)->(C,R,0) be a real function singularity with a real deformation F whose real parameter space R^k is divided into chambers by the real total discriminant of non-Morse functions and functions with critical value 0. For a non-simple real singularity, formal surgeries can be performed on collections of critical values together with their intersection matrix and additional real Morsification invariants, and these formal surgeries can be composed in arbitrary chains. What obstructions determine whether such chains of formal changes are realizable by actual paths in the real parameter space R^k?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,\mathbb{R}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C},\mathbb{R},0)$ be a real isolated function singularity, and let $F:(\mathbb{C}^n\times\mathbb{C}^k,\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^k,0)\to(\mathbb{C},\mathbb{R},0)$ be a real (mini-versal) deformation of $f$ depending on parameters in $\mathbb{R}^k$. Inside $\mathbb{R}^k$, the real total discriminant — i.e. the union of parameter values for which the corresponding function is non-Morse together with parameter values for which $0$ is a critical value — separates $\mathbb{R}^k$ into open chambers. Crossing a wall of this discriminant from one chamber to a neighboring one induces a "surgery" on the combinatorial data of a real Morsification (the collection of real critical values, the intersection matrix on the vanishing cycles, and the additional set of topological invariants of a real Morsification).

For a non-simple real singularity, one may consider purely formal surgeries on this combinatorial data (collections of critical values endowed with their intersection matrix and the additional real Morsification invariants), and one may compose such formal surgeries in arbitrary finite chains. Call such a chain realizable if it arises from an actual continuous path in $\mathbb{R}^k$ avoiding generic strata of the discriminant.

Determine the obstructions that decide whether a given chain of formal surgeries on the combinatorial data of a real Morsification of a non-simple real singularity is realizable by an actual path in the real parameter space $\mathbb{R}^k$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. An enumeration algorithm for such chains of formal surgeries was implemented (Vassiliev, 2002), and computational checks for all corank-2 singularities with Milnor number ≤ 11 found no non-realizable formal surgery, but no general theorem identifying the obstructions has been published. No subsequent work resolving the obstruction question for non-simple real singularities was located.
